subject_line: A Doctor Lost 70 Pounds Eating Steak
opening: Happy weekend, carnivores. This week got weird in the best way. A K-pop idol announced she's eating carnivore, the protein-first food pyramid went mainstream, and we've got a deep dive on the coffee debate that's been splitting the community for months. Grab your steak and let's catch up.

blog_teasers.title: Carnivore and Coffee: The Debate That Won't Die
blog_teasers.teaser: Some people say coffee saved their mornings on carnivore. Others say ditching it changed everything. Sarah breaks down the actual research on caffeine, cortisol, and gut health so you can stop guessing.

blog_teasers.title: The Carnivore Morning Routine That Fixed My Workouts
blog_teasers.teaser: Marcus was dragging through his first hour of training until he rearranged three things about his morning. The fix was simpler than he expected, and it might work for you too.

blog_teasers.title: K-Pop Star Goes Carnivore and the Comments Are Unhinged
blog_teasers.teaser: When a major K-pop idol posted her all-meat meals, fans had opinions. Lots of opinions. Chloe breaks down the reaction and why this moment matters more than you think.

whats_trending:
The protein-first food pyramid is here: A redesigned food pyramid that puts protein at the base went viral this week. Nutritionists are split, but the carnivore community is calling it a win. After decades of grain-heavy guidance, seeing meat and eggs at the foundation feels like a turning point.

Meatstock 2026 sold out: 1,600 people packed into one room to talk about meat. The lineup included Dr. Shawn Baker, Dr. Anthony Chaffee, and a live cooking demo that had the whole venue smelling like ribeye. If you missed it, Chloe's got a full recap dropping next week.

K-pop meets carnivore: A major K-pop star shared her all-meat meals on social media and the fan reaction was... a lot. The crossover nobody predicted is bringing a whole new audience to this way of eating, and the comment sections are genuinely entertaining.
community_pulse: The coffee conversation exploded this week and I don't think it's settling down anytime soon. Some folks are reporting better sleep and steadier energy after dropping caffeine entirely. Others swear black coffee with a side of butter is non-negotiable. Here's what I find interesting: the research on caffeine and cortisol response varies a lot depending on your baseline stress levels and how long you've been adapted. It's not a simple yes or no answer, and that's exactly why we wrote a full breakdown for you this week. On another note, beef tallow keeps gaining ground as the cooking fat of choice. I've seen more people ditching seed oils for rendered fat in the last month than in the entire past year. The trend is real and the science backs it up.
looking_ahead: Next week we're going deep. Sarah's tackling the carnivore and alcohol question everyone keeps asking about. Marcus has a rendered fat vs. butter cooking protocol that'll change how you think about your pan. And we've got a full guide on body recomp, losing fat and building muscle on carnivore at the same time. It's going to be a big one.
